entities.summary:
Giovanni da Nola (1478–1559), also known as Giovanni Merliano, was an Italian sculptor and architect of the Renaissance, active in Naples.

Da Nola was born in Naples, the son of a wealthy merchant, and trained in the arts from a young age.

In 1503, he was appointed as the head sculptor of the Cathedral of San Gennaro in Naples, a position he held until his death in 1558.

During his career, da Nola created numerous works of art, including sculptures and architectural designs, many of which are still preserved today.

Da Nola's work had a significant impact on the development of Neapolitan Renaissance architecture and sculpture, influencing a generation of artists.

The city of Naples lost a master craftsman with his passing, leaving behind a legacy of artistic excellence that continues to inspire and educate.

The Cathedral of San Gennaro, where da Nola spent the final years of his life, remains one of the most iconic landmarks in Naples, a testament to the enduring power of his art.

Da Nola's work continues to be celebrated for its technical skill, emotional depth, and enduring beauty, a lasting tribute to the artist who brought light and joy to a city he loved.
